newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas says load factor rises in April.
newsitem.headline: Qantas says load factor rises in April.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd's group load factor, which measures how full its planes are with paying passengers, rose in April and was higher for the financial year (July-June) to date than a year earier, Qantas' traffic statistics showed on Wednesday.
Qantas' group revenue seat factor (RSF) rose to 72.8 percent in April from 71.5 percent in April 1996 and its year-to-date RSF rose to 73.5 percent from 72.9 percent.
For domestic business, the RSF in April was unchanged on a year earlier at 79.1 percent, and year-to-date RSF was down at 78.4 percent from 79.5 a year earlier.
However, Qantas' international RSF rose in April to 71.6 percent from 69.6 percent and year-to-date RSF was up at 72.5 percent from 71.4 percent.
Domestic passengers rose to 802,000 in April from 795,000 a year earlier, with year-to-date passengers at 8.091 million against 7.878 million.
International passengers rose 5.3 percent in April to 538,000 from 511,000 a year ago, and year-to-date passengers were up 8.2 percent at 5.643 million from 5.213 million.
Group passengers rose to 1.539 million in April from 1.477 million, and year-to-date passengers grew to 15.638 million from 14.709 million.
Shares in Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, rose three cents on Wednesday to close at A$3.13.
Qantas' major competitor Anset Australia, owned jointly by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd, does not issue monthly traffic figures.
